channel.title: Zagzy Link — Journal
channel.description: Essays on interface craft, design systems, performance, and building products for real bandwidth.

item.title: The Subtle Art of Micro-interactions in Modern Web Design
item.description: Micro-interactions are the smallest unit of product craft. Here is how I decide which ones earn their place — and which are just decoration.

item.title: Why Minimalist Architecture Inspires Clean User Interfaces
item.description: Structural minimalism is a transferable discipline: load-bearing lines exposed, emptiness treated as an active material, ornament removed until only intent remains.

item.title: Structuring Design Systems for Long-term Scalability
item.description: A design system is a repository, not a Figma file. Tokens are the atomic layer that keeps ten platforms consistent for years instead of weeks.

item.title: Balancing Form, Function, and Brand Narrative
item.description: Beautiful and broken, or fast and forgettable — both are failures. The craft is in the synthesis, and the synthesis is an engineering decision as much as a design one.

item.title: Writing for the Web: Editing Is the Design
item.description: Interface copy is the interface. Most layout problems I have been handed turned out to be editing problems wearing a layout costume.

item.title: Interface Performance Is a Design Decision
item.description: Every interaction that ships commits to a render budget. Decide the budget in the design phase, or the browser will decide it for you.

item.title: Notes on AI-assisted Engineering Without Losing the Craft
item.description: Generated code is a draft, not a decision. The parts of this job that resist automation are exactly the parts that were always the job.

item.title: Building for Real Bandwidth: Lessons from Shipping in Nigeria
item.description: Designing for unreliable networks is not a compromise on quality. It is the most honest performance critique you will ever receive.

item.title: On Longevity: Building Products That Outlive Their Launch
item.description: Launch is the cheapest day in a product’s life. What survives is what was designed for maintenance by someone who was not in the room.
